news.headline: NeurAxis Announces Medical Coverage Policy Milestone, Expanding Access to Over 18 million additional Covered Lives
NeurAxis to Participate in the Lytham Partners Fall 2026 Investor Conference
NeurAxis at iAccess Alpha Conference: VA Reps Hired, Nearly 30 Payer Policies, 2026 Revenue Pace of $7-8M
news.summary: At the September 15 virtual presentation CEO Brian Carrico said NeurAxis has hired 10-12 commission-only (1099) reps for the VA Federal Supply Schedule channel, now holds nearly 30 medical policies covering over 100 million lives (Anthem ~40M, 11-13 BCBS plans, Molina ~5M), and is on pace for $7-8M of 2026 revenue even without new policy wins, with cash-flow breakeven seen at roughly $13-14M annual revenue. Management put shares outstanding at 13.6M (20.4M fully diluted incl. 3.7M Series B preferred expected to convert after the 8.5% coupon ends Dec 31) and said 2-3 more major payers could lift revenue up to 10x; note the recap's ~$4M mid-year cash figure conflicts with the $8.3M reported in the Q2 10-Q.

news.headline: Neuraxis Gains Nearly 137% in a Year: What's Driving the Stock?
news.summary: Zacks credits the 136.6% one-year gain (vs. a 12.2% industry decline) to the Category I CPT code, broader written payer coverage, the VA contract with early reorders prompting dedicated VA sales coverage, and the functional dyspepsia label expansion. It flags incomplete payer and Medicaid fee-schedule coverage, ongoing losses and financing dependence, and a stretched trailing EV/Sales of 11.9x versus 5.3x for the industry.

news.headline: NeurAxis 8-K Details Completed Option Exchange Plus New Three-Year Management and Director Equity Grants
news.summary: The option-for-RSU exchange approved by shareholders on June 10 went effective July 24, cancelling 1,319,394 options and issuing an equal number of immediately vesting RSUs. On August 13 the compensation committee added three-year-vesting grants priced at $6.28 - 193,329 RSUs to Brian Carrico, 141,479 to CFO Timothy Henrichs, 133,341 to Adrian Miranda and 135,906 to Thomas Carrico - plus one-time share awards to independent directors Kristin Ferge (31,134), Bradley Watkins (26,073) and Jane Keyser (26,073) after a consultant found pay below market.

news.headline: NeurAxis Reports Record Q2 2026 Results: Revenue Up 116%, but EPS Miss and Going-Concern Language Persist
news.summary: Q2 revenue rose 115.7% year over year to $1.93M on 60% unit growth, gross margin expanded 230 basis points to 85.9%, and average selling price rose 28% to $992 as the Category I CPT code 64567 pushed more devices to full reimbursement. On the call management said 24 commercial insurers now have formal PENFS policies covering over 100 million lives and prior-authorization approvals improved to 31% from 12%, but EPS of -$0.19 missed the -$0.16 consensus, opex jumped 53% to $3.8M, and the going-concern qualification stayed in place despite $8.3M of cash at June 30.

news.headline: Resale Prospectus for 1.92 Million Insider and Employee Shares Goes Effective, Adding Potential Supply
news.summary: The S-3 filed July 23 was declared effective August 3 and the final prospectus followed on August 6, registering 1,923,194 shares for resale by selling stockholders - 849,212 already-issued shares, 923,776 underlying RSUs and 150,206 director service shares. That is about 15% of the 12,477,309 shares outstanding as of July 22 and includes stakes held by CEO Brian Carrico (213,445 registered), CFO Timothy Henrichs (231,591) and former director Christopher Brown (792,837).

news.headline: NeurAxis Expands Payer Coverage with New Policies, Adding Over 500,000 Covered Lives
news.summary: New medical policies for PENFS added more than 500,000 covered lives, expanding access to IB-Stim for beneficiaries in the Mid-Atlantic region. CEO Brian Carrico framed the regional wins as building momentum toward comprehensive nationwide written policy coverage while talks with the nation's largest payers continue.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings (estimated date)
catalysts.detail: Consensus/data-provider estimates point to roughly November 17, 2026 for the Q3 report, continuing the usual cadence (Q1 on May 12, Q2 on August 11); NeurAxis has not yet issued its own "host a call" press release confirming the date. Key tests: whether revenue tracks the $7-8M full-year pace management reiterated on September 15 (implying $3.5-4.5M in H2 versus $3.5M in H1), whether ASP keeps climbing from $992 toward the ~$1,200 list price, the first read on orders from the newly hired 10-12 VA reps, cash burn against the $8.3M June-30 balance as W-2 headcount heads to ~15 by year-end, and whether the going-concern qualification can be dropped.

catalysts.label: Major national payer coverage decision
catalysts.detail: Talks with two large commercial payers gained traction in Q2 and management remains cautiously optimistic about a coverage win in H2 2026 or early 2027. On September 15 the CEO said adding just 2-3 more major payers could lift revenue as much as 10x given 2-3 month patient wait times, and hospitals generally want roughly 70% of their population covered before adopting broadly. NeurAxis now counts nearly 30 medical policies covering over 100 million lives (Anthem ~40M); a top-five national payer would be a step change versus the usual 0.5-1.25 million-life regional additions.

catalysts.label: RED commercial ramp and additional PENFS indications
catalysts.detail: The Rectal Expulsion Device received FDA 510(k) clearance in December 2024 as a screening tool for chronic constipation and pelvic floor dysfunction in adults and already carries a Category I CPT code with Medicare and broad commercial coverage, so it needs distribution rather than reimbursement work. Separately, PENFS is in randomized trials for post-concussion syndrome, cyclic vomiting syndrome, opioid-sparing post-operative pain and fibromyalgia, any of which could support a future 510(k) label expansion beyond the pediatric FAP/functional dyspepsia franchise.

catalysts.label: Series B preferred coupon ends, conversion expected
catalysts.detail: The Series B preferred carries an 8.5% coupon that expires December 31, 2026, and management said on September 15 it expects the roughly 3.7 million preferred shares to convert into common stock afterward. Conversion removes the preferred dividend drag (about $0.19M per quarter in Q2) but lifts common shares from 13.6M toward the 20.4M fully diluted count, which matters for per-share valuation.

catalysts.label: Broader VA expansion decision
catalysts.detail: The first 10-12 commission-only VA territory reps were hired on schedule for the mid-September target, each covering one to three of the roughly 180-200 VA hospitals and community care centers reachable under the Federal Supply Schedule contract live since December 1, 2025. Management has said results from this initial cohort will inform whether to expand the VA sales effort more broadly in early 2027, making Q4 2026 VA orders the key data point.

catalysts.label: State Medicaid adoption of CPT 64567
catalysts.detail: Management said on September 15 that 25-30 states have loaded CPT code 64567 onto their Medicaid fee schedules under EPSDT, while another 20-25 states still have no payment methodology, blocking coverage for those beneficiaries even though the Category I code has been in effect since January 1, 2026. Each additional state unlocks a reimbursed patient pool that is disproportionately important in pediatric gastroenterology, and the 2027 fee-schedule update cycle is the next broad opportunity.

catalysts.label: Covered lives above 200 million
catalysts.detail: Management reiterated on the Q2 call that it expects to exceed 200 million covered lives by the end of 2027, roughly doubling from the 100 million-plus reached today, with the CEO saying he would be highly disappointed to miss that level and framing the next 15-18 months as a strong run. Reaching it would effectively cover the serviceable market and requires a steady cadence of payer-policy wins, ideally anchored by at least one national payer.

pulse: NRXS is trading around $5.75-5.90 on September 16, essentially flat versus the $5.79 close two days earlier, for a market cap near $72-79M depending on whether the 12.5-13.6M basic share count is used, still up roughly 90-140% over the trailing year but well off the $9.33 52-week high, on a stretched ~12x trailing EV/Sales with Craig-Hallum's Buy and $13 target the lone active coverage. No new company-specific news has emerged since the September 15 iAccess Alpha conference presentation and accompanying Zacks momentum piece; the story remains the incremental read-through from that update - 10-12 VA reps hired on schedule, nearly 30 payer policies covering over 100 million lives, and a $7-8M 2026 revenue pace guided without needing new wins. The thesis still hinges on landing one of the two large commercial payers in negotiation and further Medicaid states loading CPT 64567, set against the going-concern language, $8.3M of June-30 cash, the 1.92M-share resale overhang and 3.7M Series B preferred shares expected to convert after December 31, with Q3 earnings (estimated mid-to-late November, unconfirmed) the next hard catalyst.
